## Motivation

On CPU, sglang auto-computes mem_fraction_static from total host memory and does not honor container cgroup memory limits. This makes a single server reserve a huge KV-cache pool regardless of the actual model size, and makes it impossible to run multiple sglang containers on one host safely.

## Modifications

Added a `get_available_cpu_memory` function which tries to retrieve the cgroup memory limit from `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max`. Existing CPU mem acquisition approach ` psutil.virtual_memory().total` is used as a fallback.

- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

**python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py:814**
* If `memory.max` is readable but `memory.current` is unreadable or malformed, this fallback returns host-wide `psutil.virtual_memory().used`, and line 496 subtracts it from the per-container limit. Those values have different scopes, so a sibling container can make the result negative or severely understated; keep the capped path on a cgroup-scoped value or fall back to host math when usage cannot be read.
**python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py:4348**
* Because `allowed_cpus` is now the gate for retaining a node, a cpuset that exposes no CPU selected as the physical representative (for example, a logical-thread-only affinity) makes `get_cpu_ids_by_node()` return `[]`. The CPU branch at line 502 then divides by zero during `get_available_gpu_memory("cpu", ...)`. Please add an empty-node fallback or guard before this filtering can yield an empty list.
**python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py:4348**
* These entries are keyed by the actual NUMA IDs, but `get_cpu_memory_capacity()` later discards those IDs and reads `node0` through `node(n-1)`. With only NUMA node 1 allowed, the uncapped fallback therefore reports node 0's `MemTotal`, producing the wrong capacity on socket-pinned bare-metal containers. Preserve the node IDs or make the capacity calculation iterate the retained keys.

**python/sglang/srt/model_executor/cpu_graph_runner.py:731**
* This replaces a cheap `psutil.virtual_memory()` read with `get_available_gpu_memory("cpu", ...)`, which recomputes NUMA topology by spawning `lscpu`. Because it is inside the loop, every captured batch size now incurs a topology subprocess; large CPU graph capture lists will pay this overhead repeatedly. Cache the topology/count for the capture or query the memory once per capture.

* `_read_cgroup_memory_max()` is documented as best effort for unreadable files, but `open()`/`read()` can raise other `OSError` subclasses (for example, `IsADirectoryError` or an I/O error), which are not caught here and abort startup instead of using the host fallback. ## Motivation

On CPU, sglang auto-computes mem_fraction_static from total host memory and does not honor container cgroup memory limits. This makes a single server reserve a huge KV-cache pool regardless of the actual model size, and makes it impossible to run multiple sglang containers on one host safely.

## Modifications

Added a `get_available_cpu_memory` function which tries to retrieve the cgroup memory limit from `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max`. Existing CPU mem acquisition approach ` psutil.virtual_memory().total` is used as a fallback.
